scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, across 9,200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Disputed bills break down by read type as 1,240 ESTIMATED and 1,785 ACTUAL, per billing-db.

F-03.statement: Billing-db tariff change log shows zero recorded tariff changes.

F-04.statement: CRM dispute response times across 2,440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, to be executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: Route-log lagging_routes query identified 14 distinct routes behind schedule, each with a distinct completion value (e.g., R-00 at 0.70 completion).

F-08.statement: Billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle query returned 320 accounts with estimated bills last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes, with fields limited to account_id and route.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The August-September dispute surge is driven by slow/inadequate ticket response capacity, so an auto-answering AI agent targeting ticket throughput would resolve it, as SH-CS frames it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced errors that produced incorrect bills, driving disputes.

H-AMI-DATA-QUALITY.statement: Vendor-side AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation problems are feeding bad or estimated reads into billing, causing wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Degradation in the contracted manual field meter-reading process (missed/late reads) is increasing estimate substitution and causing wrong bills.

H-SEASONAL-USAGE.statement: Bills are substantively correct and the dispute surge reflects a legitimate rise in consumption (e.g., seasonal) that customers perceive as erroneous, rather than any process defect.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log shows field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts — a real shortfall in the contracted manual reading process. This is consistent with missed/late reads increasing estimate substitution, a candidate driver of wrong bills during the same period as the dispute surge.

Billing-db shows disputed bills split 1,240 ESTIMATED vs 1,785 ACTUAL, so the majority (59%) of disputed bills involve ACTUAL, not estimated, reads. This caps how much estimate-substitution causes (missed field reads, estimate-flagging AMI issues) can explain the dispute surge, since most disputed bills were never estimated in the first place.
Billing-db's tariff change log returned zero records, meaning no tariff/pricing change was logged, which rules out a tariff change as an explanation for the wrong bills behind the dispute surge.
CRM dispute response-time data (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, 2,440 tickets) shows ticket response is currently within SLA, not breaching it, despite the dispute surge.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD attributes the manual-read route shortfall to being three readers short since July, claiming late routes cause those customers to receive estimated bills; this is an unverified causal claim from a stakeholder incentivized toward headcount increase, offering a mechanism consistent with the completion-rate gap already observed in E-01.

CRM dispute_volume_monthly shows disputes at 610 (Jun) and 590 (Jul), then jumping to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) — confirming the dispute surge began in August and roughly doubled from the Jun-Jul baseline. The data confirms surge timing/magnitude but is silent on which process defect caused the underlying wrong bills.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year, which echoes rather than adds new information to the already-recorded tariff_change_occurred assertion. As a non-authoritative stakeholder claim it corroborates but does not independently verify the ruling-out of a tariff change as a dispute-surge driver.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 confirms via the service contract that field dispatch route priority changes may be requested by the utility but must be executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation — this corroborates the existing K-DISPATCH authority structure rather than adding new causal information about the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log's lagging_routes query returns 14 individual routes with below-target completion (sample: R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity underneath the aggregate 88% Aug-Sep completion rate already recorded in E-01. It identifies which routes are behind schedule but does not establish any overlap with disputed-bill accounts or tickets.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query shows 320 accounts received an estimated bill in the last billing cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes, but returns only account_id and route fields with no read-type, tariff, or import-status data as the NICE_TO_HAVE work item anticipated. This gives a bare count/footprint of recent estimation activity with no linkage to disputed tickets, disputed-bill read types (E-02), or the 14 lagging routes (E-09), so it cannot establish how much estimate substitution contributes to the dispute surge.

problem_definition.root_problem: CRM dispute tickets roughly doubled from a Jun-Jul baseline (~600/month) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-06). This is not explained by slow ticket handling (median response 1.6d, p90 2.8d, within the 3.0d SLA — E-04) nor by a tariff change (zero logged changes — E-03). The majority of disputed bills (59%, 1,785/3,025) involve ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02), which caps how much the confirmed field manual-read completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, 9,200 accounts — E-01) can explain, since that mechanism only produces estimated bills. The best-supported remaining mechanism is a defect in billing import/validation processing of actual meter reads introduced around the same period, producing incorrect bills on actual-read accounts and driving the dispute surge (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).
